(WebFetch extraction 22 Nov 2026 ~08:10 GMT — curl returned 403; Times of Israel, Lazar Berman with AFP, published 21 Nov 2026 23:39)

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun, in an Independence Day address on the eve of Lebanon's 83rd independence anniversary, said Iran has no right to interfere in Lebanon's internal affairs, citing its support for Hezbollah.
He urged Hezbollah to hand over its weapons and promised "no persecution, no revenge, no retribution and no spite." "The era of weapons outside the state is over."
"But friendship between countries does not give one the right to interfere in another's decisions." "What you do not accept for your own country, do not ask Lebanon to accept for its country."
"Withdraw from every inch of Lebanese territory. Stop your attacks. And return our captives."
"Occupation does not create security, and destruction does not create peace."
Hezbollah entered the war with Iran on March 2, prompting Israeli airstrikes and a ground invasion of southern Lebanon. An agreement was reached in June but sporadic fighting continues; negotiations stalled because Hezbollah has refused to disarm. Israeli forces remain in a self-declared security zone about 10 km (6 miles) deep.
